title: cell-record (computer-operating-system stratum, flat EAVT shape)
description: JSON Schema for a cell-record row as it lives on disk in a .jsonl file under the computer-operating-system stratum — the flat EAVT shape {e, a, v, t} the SPEC specifies. This is a sibling shape of the math-level cell-record at library/cell-record/cell-record.schema.json, not a refinement: the math-level schema uses a nested {cell: {subject, predicate, object}, value, t} form, whereas this COS-stratum schema flattens the cell into the e, a, v positions and elides the explicit 'value' field. The bilattice valuation is implicit 'asserted-true' per the cell-record record's frontmatter-desugaring rule, unless v is overridden as a bilattice pair {t,f}. Projection to the math object: cell = (e, a, v), value = asserted-true (default), t = t.

e.description: Entity-slug — the subject of (s, p, o). Same slug pattern as math-level predication-cell.subject. Permits the basename pattern used across the OS plus the wider 'display name' form (with spaces and punctuation) that some entity records use as their slug. POSIX-pathname-safe when no spaces are present.

a.description: Transformer-gerund-slug — the predicate of (s, p, o), named by a gerund whose realization is an ESM Node transformer module. Must be a slug containing the substring 'ing' (the gerund discipline).

v.description: Object of (s, p, o). Either a structure-slug (the common case), a literal of any JSON type (string/number/boolean/array/object/null), or a bilattice pair {t,f} when explicitly overriding the default asserted-true valuation.

t.description: ISO-8601 transaction-id (date-time). Together with e, a, v, content-addresses the row.

stratum.description: Optional stratum tag: 'asserted' (stratum-0, in-flight input), 'saturated' (stratum-1, sigma-fired), 'settled' (stratum-2, delta-stabilized).

derived-from.description: Optional list of prior row cell-ids this record depends on. Records dependency under the closure-rule that fired.

derived-via.description: Optional gerund-slug naming the closure-rule that produced this record from its derived-from set.
